"use client"; import React, { use } from "react"; import { ChevronLeft, ChevronRight, CheckCircle, Circle } from "lucide-react"; import Link from "next/link"; import { useRouter } from "next/navigation"; import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"; import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, } from "@/components/ui/accordion"; import { useGetCourseByIdQuery } from "@/lib/feature/courses/coursesApi"; export default function CourseDetailPage({ params }: { params: Promise<{ courseId: string }> }) { const router = useRouter(); const { courseId } = use(params); const { data: response, isLoading } = useGetCourseByIdQuery(courseId); const apiCourse = response?.data; const course = apiCourse ? { title: apiCourse.courseName || "Untitled Course", description: apiCourse.description || "No description provided.", progress: (apiCourse as any).progress || 0, mastery: (apiCourse as any).mastery || 0, modules: apiCourse.modules?.map(m => ({ id: m.id, title: m.moduleTitle || `Module ${m.moduleNumber}`, duration: "N/A", // Not all APIs have this yet lessons: m.studyTopics?.map((t, idx) => ({ id: `${m.id}-lesson-${idx}`, title: t.topic_name, type: "Topic", duration: "N/A", completed: false, })) || [] })) || [], masteryRequirement: apiCourse.masteryRequirement || 0, averageMastery: (apiCourse as any).averageMastery || 0, modulesCompleted: (apiCourse as any).modulesCompleted || 0, lessonsCompleted: (apiCourse as any).lessonsCompleted || 0, assessmentsCompleted: (apiCourse as any).assessmentsCompleted || 0, } : null; if (isLoading) return
Loading course details...
; if (!course) return
Course not found
; return (
{/* Header */}

{course.title}

{course.description}

{/* Learning Overview */}

Learning Overview

Progress {course.progress}%
Mastery Level {course.mastery}%
{/* What to do next */}

What to do next

Continue with your next lesson:

{/* Syllabus */}

COURSE SYLLABUS

Modules, lessons, and assessments

{course.modules.map((module) => (
{module.title} {module.duration}

Lessons

{module.lessons.map((lesson) => (
{lesson.completed ? ( ) : ( )}
{lesson.title} {lesson.type}
{lesson.duration} ))} {!module.lessons.length && (
No lessons available yet.
)}
))}
{/* Footer Stats - matching the bottom of the design */}
{course.masteryRequirement}%
Mastery Requirement
{course.averageMastery}%
Average Mastery
{course.modulesCompleted}
Modules Completed
{course.lessonsCompleted}
Lessons Completed
{course.assessmentsCompleted}
Assessments Completed
{/* Floating continue button if needed or bottom action */}
); }

Error: Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders

Effects are intended to synchronize state between React and external systems such as manually updating the DOM, state management libraries, or other platform APIs. In general, the body of an effect should do one or both of the following:
* Update external systems with the latest state from React.
* Subscribe for updates from some external system, calling setState in a callback function when external state changes.

Calling setState synchronously within an effect body causes cascading renders that can hurt performance, and is not recommended. (https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect).
